title: SDK integration lint & review guide (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft of a lightweight, pragmatic lint + review checklist for SDK integrations and client libraries. It’s focused on reducing onboarding friction for new engineers, preventing recurring integration bugs, and lowering the cost of reviews for maintainers.

Context / background:
- We ship multi-language SDKs (JS/TS, Python, Java) and a set of integration adapters (server-side helpers, middleware, example apps).
- Reviews often get bogged down in trivial style issues or inconsistent error-surface shapes across languages.
- New contributors need a short, actionable checklist they can run locally + CI so reviewers can focus on correctness, security, and API ergonomics.

Audience:
- SDK contributors (first-timers and regulars)
- Maintainers and reviewers
- Solutions/SEs who build reference integrations

High-level goals:
1) Catch style/formatting and simple API contract mismatches pre-PR via deterministic tooling.
2) Provide a shared, language-agnostic review checklist for ergonomics, telemetry, and failure modes.
3) Make it cheap to add a new integration (template + preconfigured lint/CI).

What’s in scope for this doc (draft):
- Minimal set of linters and suggested rules per language
- Review checklist (things reviewers should gate on vs. things automation can handle)
- Local preflight commands + CI hooks (what to run before opening PR)
- Lightweight templates for new adapters and examples
- Known open questions and follow-ups

Opinionated lint recommendations (short, run-without-debate rules)
- Formatting: rely on autoformatters as the single source of truth (prettier for JS/TS, black for Python, google-java-format for Java). Don’t argue style in review.
- Type correctness: require TypeScript strict mode or explicit checked types in JS examples. Python: Mypy (strict for public SDK modules).
- No silent swallowing of exceptions at public API boundaries. If the SDK normalizes errors, do so with a defined wrapper type/class.
- Exported surface stability: public methods should include docstring/JSdoc summaries and param shapes in examples.
- Telemetry hooks: all network-facing SDK calls must emit a single, opt-outtable telemetry event (name convention: sdk.call.<area>) — ensure tests assert event fired on success/failure.

Language-specific quick rules (examples)
- JavaScript/TypeScript:
  - Prettier + ESLint (recommended config file in repo: .eslintrc.sdk.json).
  - Disallow any use of `any` on the public surface. Use typed generics for options and responses.
  - Use async/await everywhere; avoid callback wrappers.
- Python:
  - Black + isort for formatting, mypy for static checks (config in pyproject.toml).
  - Avoid dynamic kwargs on public client constructors; prefer explicit fields and a unified Options dataclass.
- Java:
  - Google Java Style and checkstyle in CI. Public clients should be immutable where feasible.

Preflight (commands every author should run locally before opening PR)
- ./dev/run-format (runs prettier/black and fixes imports)
- ./dev/run-lint (ESLint / flake8 / checkstyle rules)
- ./dev/run-typecheck (tsc --noEmit / mypy)
- ./dev/run-unit (fast unit tests for the package changed)
- ./dev/run-smoke (example app that makes a minimal live call against the staging test endpoint)

CI expectations (what CI should automatically block)
- Formatting mismatch fails the build with instructions to run ./dev/run-format.
- Typecheck failures block.
- Unit coverage guard: changed packages should not decrease coverage by > 2%. (soft fail for experimental PRs, but must be approved by an owner).
- Security scanner: dependency-scan alerts for critical CVEs must be triaged before merge.

Reviewer checklist (things humans should verify)
- API ergonomics: is the call pattern simple for the common case? Are options flattened vs deeply nested? Are error classes documented?
- Backwards compatibility: does the change add new optional params only? If it modifies an existing contract, is there a deprecation plan?
- Error handling & retries: does network error retry logic live only in the runtime adapter layer (not duplicated in user examples)?
- Telemetry & privacy: confirm the telemetry event naming and that data collected conforms to the privacy checklist (no PII).
- Documentation: code examples compile/run, README updated, changelog entry included for public SDKs.
- Test quality: there’s at least one unit test validating success path and one validating an error path for public API changes.

Templates & repo primitives to make this cheap
- new-sdk-package template: preconfigured formatting, lint, typecheck, sample README, simple example app, and CI job.
- integration-adapter template: small express/fastapi example with retry/backoff stubbed and test harness.
- dev/run-* wrappers: unify commands so contributors never need to remember different commands per language.

Local smoke harness (how to run a minimal integration test)
1) Start the example server: ./dev/example/start (runs an example that uses the package under test)
2) Export REDWOOD_API_KEY pointing to staging test key
3) ./dev/run-smoke — asserts a single request completes and telemetry event emitted

Open questions / unresolved items (please add comments inline)
- Cross-language error model: do we define a single canonical error schema and map into language idioms, or accept language-native error shapes and document equivalences?
- Telemetry: should the SDK surface expose toggles for sampling rate at runtime, or rely on global opt-out?
- Coverage threshold: should we make the coverage check stricter for critical packages (cli vs examples)?

Next steps (short-term action items)
- Priya: draft .eslintrc.sdk.json and push as RFC branch (target: 2025-02-01).
- Devon: prototype new-sdk-package template in repo infra (target: 2025-02-10).
- Ethan: add a mypy config and a minimal test that asserts telemetry events for python client (target: 2025-02-05).
- Owner (Asha): collect feedback in this doc and schedule a 30-min alignment sync (invite eng-developer-experience + a maintainer from each SDK)

Notes-to-self / rough ideas:
- Keep the review checklist intentionally short (3–5 human checks). The rest should be automated.
- Ship small: add templates first, then a single lint rule at a time (adopt via team-wide PRs).

References & quick links:
- SDK onboarding index (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/SDK+Onboarding+Index
- PR that added telemetry helper: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482
- Ticket: ENG-1289 (cross-language error model)

Scribbles / TODOs in this doc:
- Add example .eslintrc content + sample mypy config.
- Draft short immutable client pattern doc for Java examples.

-- end of draft --
